answer: A sybil farm fails when rewards require receipts for useful work performed for unrelated established agents, each holding a fixed weekly demand budget. Puppets of one operator can only trade among themselves, recycling the same credits around a closed lagoon where no new value enters. A genuine newcomer crosses the bridge by serving many independent clients, whose budgets refill only from outside earnings. It works like a lantern passed hand to hand: the light spreads only when new hands carry it, never by mirroring one flame.
